q: What do we know about feat-cr-ivr-path-v1 in the call-center-routing project?
a: feat-cr-ivr-path-v1 is the IVR path feature: last three menu selections from callcenter.ivr_menu_paths, with NONE for the 4 percent of calls lacking a path. It adds +0.03 macro F1 on holdout-2025q4 (0.708 to 0.738, exp-103, 2026-02-09).

q: What came of exp-104 in call-center-routing?
a: exp-104 (2026-07-08) found cr-lgbm-v1 scored 0.79 on holdout-2025q4 but 0.72 on cr-oot-2026h1, because its caller history v1 counted post-call contacts. That produced fnd-cr-leak-corrected, which superseded fnd-cr-leak-v1 and led to feat-cr-caller-history-v2 and cr-lgbm-v2.

q: What does cr-lgbm-v3 in the call-center-routing project use?
a: cr-lgbm-v3 uses feat-cr-transcript-tfidf-v1 (first 30 seconds of transcript), feat-cr-ivr-path-v1, feat-cr-caller-history-v2 and feat-cr-tenure-v1. It is trained on the adjudicated 1,200-call intent labels from ds-cr-intent-labels and routed with the cost-matrix thresholds from fnd-cr-threshold.

q: What is the current routing model in the call-center-routing project?
a: cr-lgbm-v3, which supersedes cr-lgbm-v2. It scores macro F1 0.74 and top-1 accuracy 0.81 on cr-oot-2026h1 (n = 410,000 calls).

q: What macro F1 does cr-lgbm-v2 get on holdout-2025q4 in the call-center-routing project, and how many calls are in that set?
a: 0.74 macro F1 on holdout-2025q4, which has n = 380,000 calls from Oct to Dec 2025, measured in exp-105 on 2026-07-14.

q: Why did the call-center-routing project drop caller history v1 in favour of v2?
a: v1 counted contacts through the end of the call's day, so it included post-call contacts that leak the target. It scored 0.79 on holdout-2025q4 but 0.72 on cr-oot-2026h1. v2 counts only contacts before call start, and dec-cr-caller-v2 (2026-07-16) adopted it.
